relationships.subject: IL-10
relationships.evidence_quote: Bath application of IL‐10 (100 ng/ml) reduced the increased frequency and amplitude of mEPSCs from the SNL rats but not sham rats.

relationships.subject: exenatide
relationships.evidence_quote: Nerve injury significantly increased the frequency and amplitude of mEPSCs, both of which were fully rescued by the bath application of exenatide (1 μM).

relationships.subject: β-endorphin
relationships.evidence_quote: Intrathecal injections of IL-10, exenatide, and the μ-opioid receptor (MOR) agonists β-endorphin and DAMGO inhibited thermal hyperalgesia and mechanical allodynia in neuropathic rats.

relationships.subject: spinal microglia
relationships.evidence_quote: spinal microglial expression of β-endorphin mediates IL-10- and exenatide-induced inhibition of glutamatergic transmission and pain hypersensitivity via presynaptic and postsynaptic MORs in spinal dorsal horn

relationships.subject: spinal nerve ligation
relationships.evidence_quote: Patch‐clamp recordings showed that both frequency and amplitude of mEPSCs were significantly increased compared with sham group

key_findings: Intrathecal IL-10 and exenatide reduced SNL-induced allodynia/hyperalgesia and suppressed enhanced lamina II mEPSCs but not mIPSCs; effects blocked by β-endorphin antiserum, CTAP and minocycline.
Spinal microglial β-endorphin acting on MORs mediates IL-10/exenatide inhibition of glutamatergic transmission in neuropathic pain.
